title: SLO Creation Wizard + Incident Context Cards with On‑Call Quick Actions
creator: Rita Alvarez
description:
Summary:
Design a guided SLO creation experience and an incident context card that surfaces linked postmortems, runbooks, and one-click on‑call actions (transfer, acknowledge, assign). The goal is to reduce cognitive load during incidents and make alert setup less error-prone for product engineers. This ticket covers: the SLO wizard UI, templated alert rules, incident context card variants (compact/detailed), and microcopy for postmortem and handoff links.

Background:
Teams frequently create SLOs without a clear mapping to alert triggers or runbooks. In incidents we see slow handoffs (manual copying of links to Slack), missed postmortems, and unclear ownership. Console dashboards currently surface alerts and SLOs separately; we want a connected flow so an SLO can suggest alert templates and incident cards surface the most relevant artifacts.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-setup for SLO+alert by 40% through templates and defaults.
- Make on-call handoffs < 30s by providing one-click transfer and prefilled postmortem links.
- Increase postmortem creation rate by surfacing quick links in incident cards.

Scope of work:
- SLO Creation Wizard: multi-step modal (service selection → objective targets → window/weighting → suggested alerts → review & create).
- Alert Templates: rule presets (latency p95, error-rate, throughput-drop) with recommended thresholds and severity mapping.
- Incident Context Card: collapsed and expanded states; shows SLOs implicated, latest related runbook links, postmortem draft link, recent related PRs, and on-call quick actions.
- Microcopy and error states: help text for burn-rate vs. error-rate, defaults for short windows, and inline cost-estimate hint for high-frequency alerts.

Non-goals:
- Deep integration plumbing (PagerDuty token exchange) — engineering to implement connectors.
- Full localization — only EN copy included in prototype.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype (desktop) demonstrates full SLO wizard flow from start to alert suggestion
Wireframes for both compact and expanded incident context card exist and have annotations for data fields
Microcopy reviewed and approved by PM and SRE (see review_comments)
Design handoff artifacts (tokens, spacing, components) uploaded to the design library
Engineering tickets created for front-end components and API contract (ENG-3098, ENG-3112)
Usability test with 8 engineers shows median completion time for SLO+alert setup under 6 minutes
decisions: Use progressive disclosure: show only 3 recommended alert templates by default, advanced options hidden under 'Expert options'
Default SLO windows: 7d rolling for new SLOs, 30d optional; include a short explainer for tradeoffs
Incident card quick actions are client-side requests that call existing ops APIs — no new auth flows in prototype
Postmortem link is a templated link (Confluence/GDrive) prefilled with incident metadata; creation still requires user confirmation
engineering_notes: Talked with ENG-3098 owner (Priya Singh) about the suggested alert templates. Agreed on a minimal API response: {slo_id, suggested_rules[], estimated_monthly_evals}. Engineering will return cost estimate for suggested alerts in cents. PR reference: github.com/redwood/console/pull/4712 (UI stub) — add final link once merged.
research_findings: Usability baseline: internal pilot 5 engineers — pain points: unclear thresholds, missing runbook links
Qualitative: engineers prefer prefilled postmortem templates tied to incidents
Quantitative: 68% of pilot participants missed the recommended 'severity' mapping without microcopy
tasks: Produce component spec and tokens for library (Design system)
Record 1 internal usability session and capture timing metrics (UX Research)
Export prototype and upload to handoff (Figma → Zeplin/Design Library)
Coordinate with SRE for runbook link formatting and recommended fields
review_comments: 2026-02-24 | Priya (ENG): We like the templates but need an opt-out for noisy services — suggest a 'rate-limit' toggle on suggested alerts.
2026-02-26 | Marcus (SRE): Make postmortem link creation explicit; do not auto-create. Add 'Create draft' CTA that opens template with incident metadata.
2026-03-01 | Lena (PM): Add a cost hint under alert templates — small text that says 'Estimated X evals/month — $Y' so product teams can reason about noise vs. cost.
2026-03-02 | Design review: Reduced copy on compact card; move 'related PRs' into expandable section to keep card height under 160px by default.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: showing cost estimates helps decisions but relies on backend accuracy. We'll display as 'estimated' and link to calculation details.
Tradeoff: defaulting to 7d windows reduces alert noise for shorter outages but may hide long-term regressions; we recommend recommend follow-up SLOs for long-term metrics.
Accessibility: color choices follow contrast guidelines; need to validate keyboard flows for quick actions.
